errors.text_span: The chart displays a total of eleven slices representing various input material types.
errors.evidence: The chart has ten categories/slices, not eleven. The reference description confirms ten categories.

errors.text_span: A second significant slice, colored orange, represents 18.7% and is labeled "Press Release"
errors.evidence: Press Release is colored yellow in the chart, not orange. Orange is used for Social Media Post (1.1%).
External News Article is colored dark green in the chart, not blue.
Intra-agency news article is colored light blue in the chart. Dark blue corresponds to Interview.
Interview is colored dark blue in the chart, not dark green. Dark green corresponds to External News Article.
Event Posting is colored in a darker red/brown shade, not pink. Pink/light purple corresponds to Organizational Website or Organizational Report area.

"Stimulus Type" is not a data category — it is the center label of the donut chart. The 1.1% slice is labeled "Social Media Post" and is colored orange. This is a hallucinated category name and incorrect color assignment.
Email is colored light green in the chart, which is acceptable, but the reference specifies it as light green to distinguish from External News Article's dark green.
The description fails to mention that percentage labels are placed next to each slice on the outside of the chart (not within the slices), which is an important visual feature.

errors.text_span: the segments appear to be ordered roughly from largest to smallest in proportion
errors.evidence: The segments are not ordered from largest to smallest. The reference notes categories are presented in no particular order, and visually the slices are arranged around the donut without a size-based ordering.
"Stimulus Type" is the center text label of the donut chart, not a data category. The actual 1.1% category is "Social Media Post" (orange), which is missing from the description.
